pending.body: In `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs` lines 978-987, the `ShrimpHatched` event message includes only the count of hatched clutches/juveniles but does not log which suppression factors limited `hatch_rate`. In contrast, the `EggFailure` event (lines 996-1032) does diagnose causes (LowOxygen, HighTemperature, LowMinerals, etc.). When hatch_rate is mediocre (e.g. 0.4) but some clutches succeed, users see hatched events without any indication of which factor is dragging hatch success down. Add the same cause-tagging logic used for EggFailure to ShrimpHatched events when hatch_rate < some threshold (e.g. 0.8), so partial-success hatches also explain their limiting factors.

The `test_chemistry_stress_suppresses_breeding` test (reproduction_factors.rs line 445) covers TAN and NO2 independently as required by the acceptance criteria, but does not independently verify low-GH suppression of breeding. The acceptance criteria state 'Water chemistry: very low GH, high TAN, or high NO2 suppress breeding' and the reviewer unit test list does not have a separate GH test. GH is tested only indirectly via `test_all_reproduction_factors_are_named_parameters` (which verifies parameter sensitivity) and via the mineral suppression snapshot label tests. Add an explicit assertion within `test_chemistry_stress_suppresses_breeding` (or a sibling test) that shows very low GH (e.g. 1-2 dGH) independently suppresses breeding readiness below the clean baseline.
